title: SF4896 (2025-2026 Regular): Firearm transfer to an unauthorized person penalty increase provision, mandatory minimum sentence for certain transfers of a firearm to an ineligible person establishment provision and affirmative defense removal provision

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Minnesota) (gun-policy Stage 5, Minnesota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Minnesota text (Introduction, 2026-03-25; official copy, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/94/2026/0/SF/4896/versions/0/)
provenance.note: Introduced text as filed 2026-03-25; no votes recorded. Sec. 1 strikes the old two-year maximum (now three). Sec. 3 repeals subd. 4, an affirmative defense for family or household members who transferred under compulsion; its text is in the bill's appendix.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 624.7141, subd. 1): (a) A person is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for up to three years and to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000 if the person intentionally transfers a firearm to another and the person knows or reasonably should know that the transferee:
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.7141, subd. 2): A person who violates this section may be sentenced to imprisonment for up to five years and to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000 if the transferee possesses or uses the weapon within one year after the transfer in furtherance of a felony crime of violence. A person sentenced under this subdivision shall be committed to the commissioner of corrections for not less than three years or the presumptive fixed sentence under the Minnesota Sentencing Guidelines, whichever is greater.
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.7141, subd. 4): Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 624.7141, subdivision 4, is repealed.
